findings: In the central magnifier, the orange/red arrow visibly points from the money stack towards the house at left, while the teal goods arrow above also points towards that household. Read as the illustrated household/business exchange, this falsely implies payment to the household for the same goods flow. The incorrect direction remains visible at360 and680.

The surrounding four neighbouring disciplines and neutral two-way connections are useful, friendly and legible. The chart is a generic modelling/data contribution rather than evidence that mathematics determines economic causation. The books are decorative rulebook icons, not actor-used text; researchers inspect a shared model correctly.
judgments.minimalRemedy: Remove only the central internal exchange arrows, or replace them by unambiguous goods business→household and payment household→business. Preserve the good outer disciplines, people, style and landscape composition. Do not approve the original on prompt intent.

judgments.mobileDecision: All four disciplines and central inquiry remain recognisable without tiny text; necessary correction is economic direction, not size or complexity.

findings: The same red-awning bakery appears in both equally weighted panels and in the connecting motif. BWL groups inputs, production and costs around business decisions. VWL places the bakery among suppliers, another seller and households, illustrating market/economic relationships rather than macroeconomics alone.

The image is an introductory perspective illustration, not an exhaustive classification algorithm: a single household can still be a microeconomic subject and company data can support either focus, as the retained whole P cases state. No micro/macro labels or national aggregates contradict that distinction.

At360 and680, headings, repeated bakery, production icons and market actors remain visible. Small calculator/paper strokes are not required reading. Warm rounded comic style fits the Economics landscape.

The observer holds the tablet with its plain back facing the viewer; no actor is asked to read reversed text. The floating cost-document icon is a viewer-facing conceptual aid, not an actor-used notebook.
